objections.claim: The spec changes `resolveWriters` to take the *oldest* first-parent commit whose subject contains the literal `(<ticket>)`. A commit subject is untrusted, attacker-influenceable text (any PR title), and under this rule it is the *sole* input that decides which commit readiness treats as "the writer's code was on main before the window opened". A commit naming a writer ticket before the real merge — the spec's own first failure mode, citing FAFF-1109's ADR PR #1018 preceding its build — makes `before_since: true` for a commit that contains no writer code. The command's `ready` flag (the artifact FAFF-1261 will use to switch on refusal) then passes a precondition it exists to enforce: writer code proven pre-window. The spec's stated mitigations are (a) "the anchors are the evidence" — but a qualifying beep-boop run with passing v0.3 anchors does not prove writer *code* provenance, which is exactly what this check adds; and (b) FAFF-1270 preflight 3a, an *operator eyeballs the shas* step in a different ticket that the spec itself notes "deliberately does not wait for" FAFF-1290 — so the command's standalone semantics ship fail-open with no in-tool control. This is a spec-caused trust decision on an input whose writer provenance the command cannot verify.
objections.evidence: `## 3. WHAT` "the resolved commit is the oldest matching first-parent commit"; `## 4. HOW` failure mode "An earlier commit names a writer before its real merge … This is accepted risk"; `## 6. DESIGN DECISION RATIONALE` "its one weakness is covered by the preflight sha check FAFF-1270 already requires"; header of `evidence-readiness.js`: "the measurable exit criterion for … FAFF-1261 may switch on refusal".
objections.predicted_consequence: `faff evidence-readiness --since <rev>` returns `ready: true` (exit 0) for a window that opened before a writer's code actually merged, because a spec/ADR/docs PR titled `(<writer-ticket>)` preceded it — FAFF-1261's enforcement cutover is then certified on a false writer precondition.
objections.disposition_rationale: Verified: a pre-merge commit naming the ticket exists as a pattern on main (FAFF-1109's ADR proposal #1018 preceded its build), so oldest-match could pass readiness falsely. Replaced oldest-match with a WRITER_MERGES pin table verified against HEAD's first-parent log and the (<ticket>) subject, falling back to today's fail-closed newest-match rule; pins change only by reviewed code, never a flag or env var. Round 2 returned approve.
